verdict.delta_sentence: Compared with the nearer gc-decomp-harness reference, this board has similarly clean tinted grouping and routing but lacks the reference’s deliberate density variation and instead relies on a rigid nine-panel grid with conspicuous horizontal dead bands.

sub_checks.name: frame_use
sub_checks.note: The nine regions span the frame, but large empty horizontal bands separate the three rows and make the composition feel more tiled than fully integrated.

sub_checks.name: corridors_and_air
sub_checks.note: Nodes and label chips generally have generous breathing room, though several labels sit tightly over long runs and the very wide canvas reduces arm’s-length text readability.

sub_checks.name: grouping
sub_checks.note: Nine clearly titled, softly tinted regions provide strong functional grouping, with each section holding only a small and readable set of nodes.

sub_checks.name: color
sub_checks.note: Section and flow colors are restrained and mostly consistent, but orange serves several concepts and outcomes are not differentiated as explicitly as the reference’s success/failure semantics.

sub_checks.name: machinery_leakage
sub_checks.note: No crosshair junctions, exposed waypoints, orphaned badges, or ambiguous wire merges are visible; arrowheads terminate cleanly.

sub_checks.name: alignment_and_rhythm
sub_checks.note: The three-column registers are strong, but repeated equal-sized panels and sparse interiors create a mechanical rhythm with less deliberate density variation than gc-decomp-harness.

sub_checks.name: edge_legibility
sub_checks.note: Crossings are effectively absent and local routes are clear, but the long green OrderConfirmed run and the dashed repair-and-replay route become near-perimeter marathons across multiple regions.

verdict.rank_order_sanity_note: The assigned scores and visual ordering agree: gc-decomp-harness ranks first at 7.5, while the board under grade and intent-classification-2 sit together at 7.0 for different visible limitations.
